text:
The amendment is likely constitutional as applied. It is neutral and generally applicable: it denies the benefit for any refusal of prescribed care except one based on excessive risk, whether the reason is religious or secular, so under *Employment Division v. Smith* it does not violate the Free Exercise Clause despite burdening the officer's religious practice. The shared note's rationale, that the amendment only conditions a benefit and so raises no Free Exercise issue at all, is the weaker ground, because *Sherbert* treated denial of benefits as a burden on religion, so the result should rest on *Smith*'s neutrality and general applicability. The spouse's best argument is that the excessive-risk exception is an individualized discretionary system that triggers strict scrutiny, but an objective exception probably does not.

CONFIDENCE: 75
